cards.notes: Hi, how are you? / Fine, thanks, and you?
Good morning, how are you? (formal) / Fine, thanks, and you? Use lei with strangers and older people.
What's your name? / My name's Anna, nice to meet you. Use your own name.
Nice to meet you. / The pleasure is mine.

cards.answer: Sono inglese, ma abito qui da un anno.
cards.notes: Where are you from? / I'm English, but I've lived here for a year. Swap in your own: americana, australiana, canadese…
Do you speak Italian? / Yes, a little. I'm learning.
How long have you been studying Italian? / For about two years.
What do you do for work? / I'm a teacher. Fare + l'/il/la + job: faccio l'infermiera, faccio il medico.

cards.prompt: Abito in via Garibaldi, al numero dodici.
cards.notes: I live at number twelve, Via Garibaldi. / Sorry, could you repeat that more slowly?
Are you here on holiday? / Yes, for a week.
See you tomorrow? / Yes, see you tomorrow.
Have a nice evening. / Thanks, you too.
